newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Stable environments key to Africa mine investments.
newsitem.headline: Stable environments key to Africa mine investments.

text.p: African countries need to create stable environments if they want foreign firms to continue committing resources to their fledgling mining industries, Golden Star Resources said on Thursday.

Adrian Fleming, Golden Star executive vice president of exploration, said although offshore spending on African mining activities had grown to $360 million in 1996 from $117 million in 1993, countries would have to work hard to sustain this trend.
Fleming told the Investing in African Mining conference investors were attracted to countries with simple and transparent laws which were not suddenly amended or changed.

Other attractions were speedy bureaucratic processes, especially when issuing licences, and minimal government intervention. A competitive legal and fiscal framework was also essential, he said, adding that Chile's success in attracting exploration dollars was due to its competitive fiscal regime.
Quoting from figures drawn up by Canada's Metals Economic Group, Fleming said Africa's top five mining investment havens were South Africa, Ghana, Burkino Faso, Tanzania and Mali.
Investment disincentives included over-zealous customs authorities who confiscated or delayed equipment being imported or mining samples being exported for analysis, Fleming said.
Other bugbears for foreign firms were the absence of foreign currency accounts in some African countries, an insistence on bank guarantees and corruption.

Golden Star, a Canadian firm, has been active in mining exploration in West Africa for 3 1/2 years. It also has a presence in South America and the Far East and has budgeted to spend around $40 million on exploration work in 1997.
